chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about two men who testified regarding a matter, and then two others came and testified to the contrary, so they differed. He said: 'A lot is cast between them, and whoever the lot falls on, upon him is the oath, and he is more deserving of the truth.'
ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence resolve conflicting testimonies from two pairs of witnesses?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the mechanism of *qur'ah* (casting lots) to resolve irreconcilable conflicts between two equal groups of witnesses, a principle foundational to Shia jurisprudence for situations where evidence is balanced. By selecting one group via lot and binding them with an oath, the Imam ensures a decisive legal outcome while acknowledging that the chosen party is 'more deserving of the truth' (*awla bi'l-haqq*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on procedural justice in the absence of clear superiority in testimony. This method highlights the practical application of divine guidance in resolving evidentiary stalemates within the community.
